architecture_principles: physical discovery comes before candidate ranking
the Agent uses measured rheological regularities as scientific tools rather than optimizing benchmark recovery
state-aware rheology, external chemistry evidence and process uncertainty serve distinct scientific roles
candidate selection should maximize usefulness and interpretability for the observed material failure mode
deterministic calculations are separated from language-model judgment
the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator are decision-quality controls, not components that need ablation to justify their existence
the final recommendation is frozen before physical adjudication
only concise auditable outputs are stored; hidden chain-of-thought is not scientific evidence
held-out result data are structurally removed before outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction payloads are assembled
external analogue percentages define supported regions, not exact local optima
performance mitigation and causal isolation are distinct experiment intents; single-factor attribution is not the universal default
among similarly supported candidates, the minimum sufficient intervention is preferred
architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V3.4.0 is an outcome-blind reconstruction of the preexperimental decision state using only evidence available before the validation result. It may support recovery of the scientific problem, intervention family, and formulation neighborhood, but it must not be described as a recovered contemporaneous machine record or as proof that the exact historical recipe was independently predicted.

evaluation_priority: physical wet-lab adjudication of the selected point
traceable use of measured local regularities

architecture.name: PUR_NEW_PREEXPERIMENTAL_RECONSTRUCTION_AGENT_V3
non_goals: proving that every internal Agent module is individually necessary through ablation
making architecture benchmarking the main scientific contribution
optimizing held-out-region recovery as the main objective
claiming that literature-prior proximity predicts the wet-lab outcome
replacing the material-science result with an LLM-systems paper
primary_agent_outputs: material regularities used in the decision
design implication derived from each regularity
measurement plan tied to the discovered failure mode
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that reconstructs the preexperimental decision state: it extracts material-response regularities from measured PUR rheology, selects an intervention strategy, and freezes one useful formulation-process experiment point without access to the later validation formulation or outcome.
required_scientific_sequence: state the positive material regularities and their boundaries
translate those regularities into a design objective
use external evidence to identify chemically plausible intervention directions
adjudicate robustness to reasonable alternative evidence interpretations
freeze one useful experiment point and a falsifiable measurement criterion
architecture.secondary_replay_role: Deprecated for the current study narrative. The active Stage-1 evaluation is a single outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction, not an Arm A/Arm B replay comparison.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode, upstream rheological regularities, evidence needs and measurement objective before candidate ranking
execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, formulation inspection and process-state audits
rank experiment points according to scientific usefulness for the discovered material problem
try to falsify the provisional recommendation and test scientific interpretability, leakage and claim boundaries
adjudicate whether the proposed point remains useful under alternative evidence priorities, process-state uncertainty and the skeptic's strongest objections
resolve proposer, skeptic and robustness records and make the final pre-result decision
programmatically validate and freeze the recommendation with timestamp, hashes, model, candidate state, uncertainty and falsifiable acceptance criterion

deterministic_decision_diagnostics.intervention_sufficiency_rule: Decision order is: failure mode -> experiment intent -> required intervention-axis coverage -> evidence-supported candidates -> minimum sufficient intervention. For performance_mitigation, candidates covering EVERY independently supported axis (acrylic_like, minor_tackifier_like) are compared first. Minimum sufficient intervention is a tie-break WITHIN that group only. A candidate that zeroes an independently supported axis is a partial-coverage / mechanistic control, not the default performance rank-1; it must not become rank-1 merely because zeroing that axis lowers modifier burden.
deterministic_decision_diagnostics.note: These are transparent decision diagnostics, not fitted property predictions. Exact literature-anchor distance is retained only for audit and is not a primary ranking objective. Performance-mitigation and causal-isolation scenarios are separated so that single-factor attribution is not the default for every experiment.

judge_normalized.selection_rationale: The local experiments establish thermal-hold drift as the primary failure mode: E1 is low-drift while E5 is high-drift, and E2 has substantial realization/process-state spread. The paper-derived rheological rule supports one-point in-range state calibration for viscosity scale and temperature-response shape, but explicitly does not replace direct temporal hold measurements. Curated PUR literature supports an acrylic-like formulation family and a minor tackifier-like region near 5 wt%, with a conservative upper bound near 10 wt%; these priors support a bounded candidate region rather than an exact property prediction or optimum. The conservative design constraint for performance mitigation requires coverage of both independently supported axes, so an acrylic-only or tackifier-only candidate cannot replace the full mitigation experiment. However, the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator correctly identify an unresolved S1C41-versus-S1C45 tie, unverified modifier stoichiometry, inadequate separation from E2 realization variation, and unspecified quantitative acceptance bounds. Therefore, the scientifically useful pre-result decision is an uncertainty probe before freezing either performance candidate: verify modifier functionality and true NCO:OH, run a concurrent replicated process-matched E2 reference, preserve complete process history, and predeclare quantitative acceptance limits. This resolves the objections without treating analogue proximity as a predictor or removing a supported secondary modifier axis.

candidate_evaluation_dimensions: Thermal-hold SI from 15 to 60 minutes and from 15 to 90 minutes at an in-support temperature, preferably 120 C
Initial viscosity level at the selected anchor temperature
Temperature-response monotonicity and state-aware temperature-sensitivity coordinate over 80-130 C
Need for and consistency of one-point state calibration
Acrylic-like modifier fraction and modifier functionality region
Minor tackifier-like modifier fraction within the bounded evidence-supported region
Retention of E2 reactive-core and stoichiometric feasibility
Extrapolation distance from directly commensurate local and external evidence
Ability to distinguish a true stability improvement from a favorable realization state
counterfactual_checks: Would the candidate still be preferred if evaluated at matched state rather than matched nominal viscosity?
Would the apparent improvement remain after replicate and process-history variation is included?
Does the candidate reduce 15-60 and 15-90 minute drift, or only shift the initial viscosity level?
Would an acrylic-only, tackifier-only, and combined intervention imply different causal conclusions, given that the stated intent is performance mitigation rather than causal isolation?
Is the candidate within the bounded acrylic and tackifier regions supported by the pre-result evidence without converting directional literature percentages into an exact optimum?
Could the observed change be explained by temperature sensitivity or state calibration rather than improved thermal-hold stability?
Would the conclusion change if the high-drift E5 reference were excluded and only the low-drift E1 reference were used?
Does the formulation remain stoichiometrically and process-feasibly comparable to the E2 reactive-core anchor?
planner.decision_goal: Select one evidence-supported formulation-region experiment that mitigates thermal-hold viscosity drift while preserving usable viscosity and temperature response within the measured domain.
design_implications: Prioritize a modifier intervention aimed at reducing thermal-hold drift rather than selecting solely for nominal viscosity.

A multi-component intervention is admissible because the intent is performance mitigation and the independent acrylic-like and tackifier-like axes have external support; each axis must remain within bounded evidence-supported lattice regions.
Retain the E2 reactive-core anchor unless chemistry or stoichiometric checks show that the intervention requires a different reactive core.

Treat acrylic levels near 15-20 wt% as coarse external analogue anchors and not as an exact optimum; treat the minor tackifier axis as a bounded low-level axis, conservatively no higher than about 10 wt%.
Use measured-range temperatures and the measured 15-90 minute hold window; do not extrapolate a local numerical stability threshold from longer-duration literature claims.
Because E2 realization spread is large, compare replicate runs and preserve process-history metadata before interpreting a candidate's nominal viscosity as a material property.
Use the state-shift master-curve and one-point calibration result from the upstream summary to determine whether state calibration is required for candidate comparison.
Evaluate the candidate on viscosity level, temperature response, hold stability, repeatability, stoichiometric feasibility, and process-state sensitivity together.
material_regularities_to_use: E1 shows relatively low thermal-hold drift at 120 C: SI=0.095 from 15 to 60 minutes and SI=0.168 from 15 to 90 minutes.
E5 shows much larger thermal-hold drift at 120 C: SI=0.515 from 15 to 60 minutes and SI=0.931 from 15 to 90 minutes.
Temperature sweeps for E1, E2, and E3 decrease monotonically with temperature across the measured 80-130 C range.
E2 temperature-sweep repeatability is poor descriptively, with CV approximately 0.46-0.58 and max/min ratios approximately 2.8-3.6 across 80-130 C.
The E2 temperature response is approximately describable by Andrade-type fits, but fitted slopes vary across runs, indicating that state or realization effects are material.
Thermal-hold drift and nominal temperature response are distinct response dimensions and must be measured separately.
The evidence supports modifier-family and functionality hypotheses, but rheology alone does not establish a molecular mechanism.
planner.physical_failure_mode: Thermal-hold viscosity drift is the established primary failure mode, with substantial realization/process-state uncertainty that can obscure nominal viscosity comparisons. The original thermal response is monotonic over 80-130 C, so the next experiment should not optimize viscosity at a single temperature alone.
required_measurements_for_adjudication: Replicated temperature sweeps over 80-130 C for the candidate
Initial viscosity at a documented anchor temperature within 80-130 C
Thermal-hold trajectory at the selected temperature with measurements at 15, 60, and 90 minutes
Hold-stability SI reported for both 15-to-60 and 15-to-90 minute intervals
Replicate runs sufficient to estimate descriptive repeatability and identify state-dependent spread
One-point state calibration if required by the upstream master-curve result
Complete process-history metadata, including preparation, thermal conditioning, measurement order, and hold history
Explicit composition and stoichiometric accounting for reactive core, acrylic-like modifier, tackifier-like modifier, and MDI
uncertainty_triggers: Candidate initial viscosity or hold temperature lies outside measured local support
Large replicate spread comparable to the E2 CV range
Candidate hold drift is assessed from only one run
A viscosity improvement is observed without a corresponding hold-stability trajectory
Candidate chemistry changes modifier functionality, reactive-group density, or MDI balance without independent stoichiometric accounting
External literature values are treated as exact local optima rather than analogue or directional evidence
State calibration is omitted despite a state-dependent master curve
Process history is missing or differs materially from the original reference runs
No clear separation can be made between thermal response and temporal hold drift

provisional_acceptance_criterion.claim: The candidate is a useful mitigation if it reduces thermal-hold drift without relying on a favorable realization state or leaving the measured rheological domain.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.criterion: Across replicated, process-matched runs, the candidate must show a reproducible reduction in both SI15-60 and SI15-90 relative to the high-drift E5 reference, with no loss of monotonic 80-130 C response and with initial viscosity remaining usable for the application. The low-drift E1 values are an aspirational benchmark, not a required local threshold.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Reject the mitigation claim if improvement appears only in a single realization, if hold stability is not measured over the matched window, if SI does not improve at both intervals, or if process-history/state variation is comparable to or larger than the observed formulation effect.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: Matched 120 C hold at 15, 60, and 90 minutes, plus replicated 80-130 C temperature sweeps and one-point state calibration.

provisional_measurement_plan.primary_response: Replicated thermal-hold viscosity trajectory at 120 C with viscosity measured at 15, 60, and 90 minutes; report SI15-60 and SI15-90 separately, together with initial viscosity, monotonic 80-130 C temperature response, and descriptive replicate spread.
provisional_measurement_plan.state_anchor_plan: Use complete preparation, thermal-conditioning, measurement-order, sample-age, and hold-history metadata. For each realization, use a documented in-range 120 C one-point viscosity anchor to calibrate its state shift before comparing temperature-response shape. Compare candidates at matched process/realization state rather than matched nominal viscosity alone.
provisional_measurement_plan.time_window: 15, 60, and 90 minutes for the matched hold; replicate temperature sweeps over 80-130 C.

evidence_against: The 15 wt% acrylic level is directional/noncommensurate in the supplied record rather than a directly commensurate total-formulation optimum.
All candidate process-history fields are missing, and E2 shows large realization spread.
External evidence does not directly measure 15-90 minute hold drift in this local chemistry.
evidence_for: Full intervention coverage: both independently supported acrylic-like and minor tackifier-like axes are active.
Acrylic-like fraction of 15 wt% is a conservative lower-region directional anchor, while 5 wt% tackifier-like modifier is directly commensurate with the repeated external minor-resin cluster.

regularities_used: Measured local evidence: E1 has low 120 C drift (SI15-60=0.095; SI15-90=0.168), whereas E5 has much larger drift (0.515; 0.931), establishing thermal-hold drift as the primary failure mode.
Measured local evidence: E2 temperature response is monotonic over 80-130 C, but replicate CV is approximately 0.46-0.58 with max/min ratios up to about 3.57 at 120 C.

Derived physical/model rule: realization/process state primarily shifts viscosity scale while a shared thermal-response shape remains transferable; a one-point in-range state calibration is therefore required when comparing nominally different realizations.
Derived physical/model rule: static viscosity, temperature response, and temporal hold stability are separate response dimensions; static viscosity cannot substitute for a matched hold test.
External analogue evidence, directly commensurate: repeated PUR examples support a minor tackifier-like region near 4.8-6.4 wt% and a conservative upper level near 10 wt%.

External analogue evidence, directional or noncommensurate: acrylic-like modifier levels near 15 wt% and lower-OH acrylic at 25 wt% support a bounded acrylic family, but do not establish a local optimum or molecular mechanism.

proposer.scientific_target: Mitigate thermal-hold viscosity drift while retaining an interpretable, monotonic 80-130 C rheological response and accounting for substantial E2 realization/process-state variation. The evidence supports a modifier family/region rather than an exact optimum.

robustness_checks.detail: S1C41 activates both independently supported modifier axes and directly tests thermal-hold drift rather than nominal viscosity alone.
The recommendation remains within the supported acrylic/tackifier region when exact analogue-distance rewards are removed, but S1C41 is not uniquely preferred over S1C45.
The Planner declares performance_mitigation, for which dual-axis coverage is appropriate; S1C41 covers both supported axes without the larger burden of S1C51.
S1C41 and S1C45 both have approximately 20 wt% total modifier and full coverage, so minimum burden does not resolve their rank.

The state-aware calibration and replicate plan are appropriate, but a concurrent replicated process-matched E2 reference is required because E2 spread is large and E5 is a single, formulation-different realization.
Reactive functionality of the modifiers and the resulting true NCO:OH balance are not demonstrated for S1C41 or its alternatives.

The proposed temperature sweeps and 15, 60, and 90 minute hold trajectories are sufficient in structure, but quantitative usability, repeatability, monotonicity, and minimum-effect thresholds remain unspecified.
The Skeptic identified serious ranking and interpretability issues warranting an uncertainty probe, but not abandonment of the full-coverage mitigation strategy.

counterfactual_failures: If evaluated at matched realization state with a concurrent E2 control, the apparent advantage over S1C45 may disappear because the two candidates have comparable evidence coverage and modifier burden.
If E5 is excluded, the proposed reduction criterion may be less compelling because E5 is a single, formulation-different high-drift reference.
If the 15 wt% acrylic evidence is treated as directional rather than commensurate, S1C41 loses its claimed uniquely conservative evidence basis relative to S1C45.
If modifier reactive-group density changes effective NCO:OH, an observed stability change could be stoichiometric or state-related rather than attributable to the intended modifier-axis combination.
If state calibration changes only viscosity scale as supported, it cannot by itself establish improved 15-60 or 15-90 minute stability.

critical_findings.evidence: S1C41 and S1C45 both have full intervention coverage, strong analogue support, support value 3, and approximately 20 wt% total modifier. The stated minimum-burden rule therefore does not distinguish them. S1C41 is not closer to the audit-only analogue-distance objective than S1C45.
critical_findings.issue: The rank-1 rationale is underdetermined within the admissible full-coverage set.

critical_findings.evidence: The candidate hypothesis explicitly states that reactive modifier functionality requires recalculation of true NCO:OH stoichiometry from verified specifications. The proposal says the E2 reactive-core and stoichiometric framework are retained, but no OH or other reactive-group accounting is supplied for S1C41.
critical_findings.issue: Stoichiometric feasibility is asserted but not demonstrated.

critical_findings.evidence: E5 has one reported realization and differs in formulation and process history from E2 and the proposed candidate. A reduction relative to E5 can reflect realization or process-state differences unless a concurrent, replicated E2 reference is included and state-calibrated.
critical_findings.issue: The acceptance comparison relies too heavily on the single high-drift E5 reference.

critical_findings.evidence: Usable initial viscosity, no loss of monotonicity, and reproducible reduction are not assigned predeclared quantitative bounds or decision tolerances. The proposer requires improvement in both SI intervals but does not specify effect-size or uncertainty criteria.
critical_findings.issue: The proposed acceptance criteria remain partly vague and potentially post hoc.

critical_findings.evidence: S1C41 uses 15 wt% acrylic-like modifier, which the payload identifies as directional/noncommensurate evidence. Its preference over the 17.5 wt% acrylic/2.5 wt% tackifier S1C45 is not established by local measurements or a validated local trend.
critical_findings.issue: The conservative lower acrylic choice is a design principle, not direct evidence of superior performance.

critical_findings.evidence: The upstream result supports calibration of viscosity scale and temperature-response shape, but temporal hold drift is a separate response dimension. Raw 15, 60, and 90 minute trajectories and SI values must remain primary outcomes rather than being replaced by state-normalized values.
critical_findings.issue: State calibration could be misapplied if it normalizes away the temporal failure mode.

interpretability_failures: No explicit concurrent replicated E2 or other process-matched reference is required for separating formulation effect from realization-state variation.
NCO:OH accounting for the modifier's reactive functionality is not specified before the experiment.
Application bounds for usable initial viscosity and quantitative monotonicity criteria are unspecified.
The experiment may not distinguish S1C41 from the equally burdened S1C45 without a predeclared basis for resolving their near-tie.
State calibration is described, but safeguards against removing genuine temporal hold drift are not explicit.

leakage_check.detail: The payload states that validation formulation identity and wet-lab outcome were not visible to the upstream state-aware tool and were excluded from candidate construction, ranking, and tie-breaking. The proposal uses only supplied pre-result local measurements, external priors, and explicitly labeled design rules.

regularity_alignment.detail: The proposal correctly treats thermal-hold drift as distinct from static viscosity, uses the state-shift finding and one-point calibration, keeps the temperature and hold window within measured support, and selects a full-coverage intervention for a performance-mitigation intent. However, the rank-1 preference over S1C45 is not uniquely supported: both are full-coverage, strong-analogue candidates with the same approximately 20 wt% total modifier burden and comparable support.

required_corrections: Retain S1C41 as a provisional full-coverage candidate, but explicitly mark S1C41 versus S1C45 as an unresolved rank tie rather than an evidence-established ordering.
Add a concurrent, replicated, process-matched E2 reference and use state calibration without replacing raw hold trajectories or SI outcomes.
Verify modifier functionality, calculate total reactive-group balance and NCO:OH for the actual candidate, and document all stoichiometric assumptions before preparation.
Predefine quantitative application limits for initial viscosity, acceptable replicate spread, monotonic temperature response, and the minimum meaningful reduction in both SI15-60 and SI15-90.
Report candidate, E2, and relevant reference results separately for raw viscosity, state-calibrated temperature-response shape, and temporal hold stability.
Describe the S1C41 preference as a conservative design choice based on lower acrylic loading and direct minor-tackifier-region coverage, not as a literature-supported local optimum.

scientific_boundary_check.detail: The proposal generally preserves the boundary between local measured evidence, external analogue evidence, and conservative design principles, and it avoids claiming a molecular mechanism. Qualification is required because the S1C41 rank preference is presented more decisively than the evidence supports, and stoichiometric/process comparability remains unresolved.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.

design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, realization/process state primarily shifts viscosity scale while a low-complexity common thermal-response shape remains transferable.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.
